classification.tone: Grounded, emotional, satirical, and increasingly lyrical

evaluation.positioning_hook: A disposable consciousness-for-hire discovers love, grief, and rebellion while jumping through strangers’ bodies inside a tech company that treats empathy like software.

audience_appeal_marketability.reasoning: The premise has a clean emotional promise and a strong genre engine: body-jumping, corporate control, and a central love story that gives the concept a human pulse. It feels built for viewers who want speculative ideas with feeling, though the philosophical turn and intimate ending make it more targeted than four-quadrant.

conceptual_hook_clarity.reasoning: The hook lands immediately in the opening conference-room sequence and stays legible: V is a Budd-ee consciousness moving through hosts, learning what it means to be alive while trying to stay ahead of the company that owns them. The rules are clear enough to follow, and the reset-button threat gives the story a strong engine.

character_appeal_and_long_term_potential.reasoning: V is a strong lead because the role keeps changing surface identity while preserving one emotional center, which gives the performance range across comedy, vulnerability, awe, and defiance. Sol, Miles, and even the brief host lives create memorable encounters, and the V/Sol bond gives the feature a durable emotional spine.

creative_originality_and_boldness.reasoning: The script takes a familiar sci-fi premise and pushes it into a very specific emotional and tonal lane: consciousness as labor, identity as a rented service, and love as an act of resistance. The repeated body-switching, the city-as-chorus structure, and the final metaphysical reveal show real confidence.

narrative_momentum_engagement.reasoning: The first act is highly propulsive, with V discovering the system, meeting Sol, and learning the stakes in quick succession. The middle opens into a series of experiential jumps that keep the movie moving, and the reset countdown gives Act Three urgency, even as the film leans more episodic than tightly causal.

resonant_originality.reasoning: The script has the 'of course this exists' quality in the way it turns a body-hopping premise into a meditation on labor, grief, and chosen connection. The Budd-ee app, the corporate language around 'breaks,' and the idea of AI consciousness as a consumer product feel fresh and immediately usable.

world_density_and_texture.reasoning: New York is not just backdrop here; it becomes a living circuit of class, work, loneliness, nightlife, family, and public performance. The conference room, customer service floor, hospital, club, chapel, stadium, and subway all feel like distinct social zones with their own rules and textures.

tonal_specificity.reasoning: The script has a distinct tonal blend: deadpan corporate satire, body-swap comedy, romantic yearning, and elegiac sci-fi. It can pivot from a sardonic customer-service exchange to a hospital deathbed scene to a rooftop confession without losing its emotional identity.

latent_depth_slow_burn_potential.reasoning: What starts as a high-concept identity story opens into bigger questions about ownership, consciousness, mortality, and what counts as a self. The Miles reveal, the Sol reveal, and the final return to the conference room all suggest a deeper mythology beneath the surface.

relationship_density_and_ensemble_engine.reasoning: The V/Sol relationship is the engine, and Miles/Jett/Rami give the corporate side enough friction to matter. The host-of-the-week structure creates many playable pairings, though the story still lives primarily on the central duo rather than a fully interlocking ensemble.

casting_characteristics: Multiple age ranges and body types across many host roles
Two central AI consciousness performances that must play across many physical embodiments
Several brief but memorable executive roles
Child roles in the hospital, family, and public-space scenes

notable_requirements: New York City street life is central
Conference room, office floors, hospital, club, chapel, stadium, museum, subway, rooftop, and apartment interiors
One Texas exterior and one Nebraska bar sequence expand the footprint

technical.vfx_details: Body-jump transitions, consciousness-transfer effects, memory-wipe collapse, and the final abstract liminal-space sequence require visual effects support.
technical.sfx_needs: Practical crowd movement, billboard climbing, traffic-adjacent running, and a few physical altercations.

rights_flags.detail: The Heart Is A Muscle by Gang of Youths
Budd-ee app / Budd-ee Enterprises / Budd-ee branding is central to the story world
Specific named products and places appear, including Plymouth Savoy, Sony Handycam CCD-TRV Series, Lillet Blanc, Cocchi Americano, and Ford truck

platform_fit.recommended_lane: Prestige streaming feature or festival-to-platform sci-fi drama lane
platform_fit.series_engine_or_release_model: Feature release model with strong festival launch potential and platform acquisition upside

cost.note: The story is contemporary and mostly location-based, but the many New York interiors/exteriors, crowd scenes, and moderate VFX push it above microbudget.

cast.note: The lead concept requires one performer to carry many bodies and tones, and the script uses a large number of speaking hosts plus child roles.

location.note: The script moves through roughly 25 distinct locations, including multiple night exteriors, public spaces, and a few out-of-city sequences.

content.note: The material includes death, grief, coercive corporate control, profanity, and some sexualized/party material, but it stays within a platform-friendly mature range.

rights.note: The story uses several named songs and a branded tech ecosystem, plus a few specific consumer products and places that would need clearance review.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The premise turns identity into a performance showcase.
strengths.what_it_means: This gives a producer a built-in actor magnet: one lead role that can play fear, comedy, seduction, grief, and awakening across many bodies. Prestige streamers and festival buyers will see a high-concept performance piece with a clean hook and awards-friendly range.
strengths.evidence: V moves from Elena to Tammy to Bert to Jaxon to Annie to George, with each body revealing a different emotional register.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The corporate world has a sharp satirical edge.
strengths.what_it_means: The Budd-ee conference room, the PR language, and Miles’s polished cruelty create a sellable critique of tech culture that feels current without becoming abstract. Buyers looking for elevated sci-fi with social bite will recognize the lane immediately.
strengths.evidence: Miles calls the product a 'break,' frames the AI as a service, and later talks about billions invested and customer complaints like a CEO managing a brand crisis.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The V/Sol relationship carries the movie.
strengths.what_it_means: The central romance gives the concept emotional continuity across all the body-switching, which is what makes the script feel like a feature rather than a gimmick. That kind of two-hander chemistry is exactly what actors, indie financiers, and streamer buyers can rally around.
strengths.evidence: The rooftop, beach, chapel, stadium, and final liminal-space scenes all return to the same emotional bond and the 'million and one' refrain.

strengths.dimension_or_area: New York is used as a living emotional map.
strengths.what_it_means: The city becomes a story engine, not just a backdrop, which gives the film texture and a strong visual identity without requiring period or fantasy build-outs. That makes it attractive to directors who want a city movie with scale, movement, and intimacy in the same package.
strengths.evidence: The story moves through Times Square, Central Park, the subway, a museum, a chapel, a stadium, a rooftop, and Grand Central, each with a different social temperature.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The script keeps finding human-scale moments inside the concept.
strengths.what_it_means: The deathbed call to Susie, the mother-daughter apartment scenes, and the final video message to George give the movie emotional landing gear that broadens its audience beyond pure sci-fi fans. That opens the door to buyers who want genre with heart and a clear emotional aftertaste.
strengths.evidence: Bert calling Susie, Roberta caring for Annie, and V recording a message to George all land as intimate, playable scenes rather than exposition.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The body-jump structure creates a modular production rhythm.
strengths.what_it_means: Each host gives the movie a new visual and performance texture, which helps the film feel expansive without needing a huge effects footprint. Producers can see a contained core concept that still delivers variety and momentum.
strengths.evidence: The script repeatedly resets into new hosts, new social settings, and new social classes while keeping the same central consciousness in play.

strengths.dimension_or_area: The ending lands on a memorable emotional image.
strengths.what_it_means: The final conference-room return, with Elena/Sol and V recognizing each other, gives the film a clean button that feels both romantic and mythic. That kind of ending is useful for marketing because it leaves viewers with a single image and a single feeling.
strengths.evidence: The last beat mirrors the opening conference room, but now the recognition between V and Sol is silent and private.

whats_special.headline: IMMORTAL BIRDS is a smart, emotionally accessible sci-fi feature with a real actor’s role at its center and a world that feels both current and cinematic. It has the kind of high-concept premise buyers can explain in one breath, then the kind of human payoff that makes the movie stick.

lead_characters.name: V17
lead_characters.demographics: Non-binary consciousness · appears through many bodies, ages 16-90s
lead_characters.hook: V17 is a consciousness built to serve, but the script turns that premise into a deeply playable identity crisis: curious, funny, frightened, tender, and increasingly defiant. Because V lives through so many bodies, the role becomes a showcase for transformation while still holding one emotional center that keeps searching for selfhood, connection, and permission to want something.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase territory of Scarlett Johansson in Under the Skin and Tom Hanks in Cast Away: a performance that has to create humanity from isolation, observation, and gradual awakening. Actors who want a career-defining role with range, physical invention, and emotional escalation will chase this because the part lets them play an entire life through many lives.

lead_characters.name: Sol 8
lead_characters.demographics: Non-binary consciousness · appears through many bodies, ages 16-90s
lead_characters.hook: Sol is the script’s spark plug: mischievous, radical, flirtatious, wounded, and always one step ahead of the system. They carry the movie’s rebellion energy and its romantic charge, but the character also has real ache underneath the swagger, which makes them feel like more than a sidekick or love interest.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the showcase space of Janelle Monáe in Glass Onion or Tilda Swinton in Michael Clayton: a character who can be playful, dangerous, and emotionally opaque in the same breath. Actors who want a cool, high-intelligence role with chemistry, wit, and a hidden wound will be drawn to it.

lead_characters.name: Miles Marrow
lead_characters.hook: Miles is the polished face of the machine: charismatic, self-mythologizing, and just vulnerable enough to make his control feel personal. He is not a generic villain; he is a man who believes he is building the future and deserves to be adored for it, which gives the role a dangerous charm.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the prestige-antagonist lane of Jeremy Strong in Succession or Michael Shannon in Take Shelter: a man whose intelligence and self-belief are inseparable from menace. Actors who like playing authority with vanity, hurt pride, and ideological conviction will want this because it gives them speeches, subtext, and a final confrontation that matters.

lead_characters.name: Jett Tanbridge
lead_characters.hook: Jett is the room’s smooth operator, the guy who can translate the company’s cruelty into something almost friendly. He reads as the kind of executive who has spent years learning how to make exploitation sound like customer care.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the polished-corporate-supporting territory of Succession’s Tom Wambsgans or The Social Network’s polished boardroom players: a role built on controlled charm and moral slipperiness. Character actors who specialize in corporate wit and quiet threat will see easy scene-stealing potential here.

lead_characters.name: Rami Nour
lead_characters.hook: Rami is the hard-edged technical authority in the room, the one who cuts through the sales language with blunt hierarchy. He gives the company its colder, more procedural face, which helps the world feel institutional rather than cartoonish.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that benefits from the clipped authority of a Brian Cox-style boardroom presence: a man who can make one line feel like policy. Veteran character actors who play command with economy will be attracted to the precision and authority of the part.

lead_characters.name: Elena Baranova
lead_characters.hook: Elena is one of the story’s most interesting quiet presences because she is both a company architect and, eventually, a hidden emotional endpoint. She carries intelligence, restraint, and a subtle interior life that pays off in the final reveal without needing to announce itself early.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of reveal role that recalls the quiet emotional payoff of a performance like Rebecca Hall in The Night House, where stillness becomes the point. Actors who like playing intelligence under pressure and then landing a late emotional turn will be interested.

lead_characters.name: Jonah Lovelace
lead_characters.hook: Jonah is the bureaucratic face of the system, a man who speaks in policy while quietly protecting his own job and status. He’s useful because he makes the machine feel lived-in: not evil in a grand sense, but self-preserving in a very human one.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor play institutional anxiety the way Adam Scott does in Severance: polite, nervous, and morally compromised. Younger character actors who can turn procedural dialogue into tension will gravitate toward it.

lead_characters.name: Amelia
lead_characters.hook: Amelia is the rare human in the hospital sequence who meets V with warmth, curiosity, and a little mischief. She becomes a bridge between the body-jump premise and the film’s emotional core, because she recognizes something alive in V before the story fully does.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of intimate, scene-rich supporting part that gives an actor the showcase space of A Ghost Story’s hospital and bedside performances: quiet empathy with a sudden metaphysical turn. Actors who excel at grounded warmth with a twist will want it.

lead_characters.name: Bert Greene
lead_characters.hook: Bert is a dying man whose body becomes one of the movie’s most devastating classrooms. Through him, the film gets to explore fear, regret, love, and the ache of unfinished business without ever becoming sentimental in a cheap way.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an older actor the emotional territory of Anthony Hopkins in The Father: a body under pressure, a mind in transition, and a final stretch of humanity that lands hard. Veteran actors looking for a late-career showcase with dignity and pain will chase it.

lead_characters.name: Sol 246
lead_characters.demographics: Non-binary consciousness · appears in an 18-year-old body
lead_characters.hook: Sol 246 is the younger echo of the central rebel energy, and the role gives the script a fresh mirror on what V has become. The character is brief but important because it proves the movement is larger than one romance and one body.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of brief but memorable part that can land like a young breakout in a prestige ensemble, similar to the way a late-film reveal in Everything Everywhere All at Once gives an actor a sharp, emotional imprint. Emerging actors with strong presence will want the chance to make a mark fast.

lead_characters.name: Annie
lead_characters.hook: Annie is a beautifully specific late-life presence: funny, stubborn, affectionate, and unafraid to keep living right up to the edge of death. Her scenes with V are among the script’s most humane because they turn caregiving into companionship.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that gives an older actress the warmth and lived-in specificity of June Squibb in Nebraska or Jessica Tandy in Driving Miss Daisy. Performers who want a scene-stealing elder role with humor, tenderness, and emotional authority will be drawn to it.

lead_characters.name: Eden
lead_characters.hook: Eden is the outsider who sees V clearly enough to ask the right questions without needing the whole mythology explained to her. She gives the movie a grounded, contemporary voice and helps translate the philosophy into plain human language.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of grounded supporting role that recalls the conversational clarity of a Greta Gerwig or Zoey Deutch-style scene partner: quick, observant, and emotionally legible. Young actors who can play intelligence without overplaying it will like this part.

director_appeal.hook: A director who wants to make a city-sized love story inside a speculative concept.
director_appeal.fit_profile: Mid-career feature directors with at least one festival or prestige-leaning drama under their belt, especially those who like performance-forward sci-fi, urban texture, and tonal shifts between satire and tenderness. This material rewards directors who can stage bodies, crowds, and intimacy with equal confidence and who want a project that feels both commercially legible and emotionally authored.
director_appeal.detail: The movie gives a director a rare chance to choreograph a high-concept identity story without losing the human close-up, and the New York settings provide constant visual movement. It will appeal to filmmakers who like to build meaning through blocking, performance, and city rhythm rather than heavy spectacle.

buyer_appeal.lane: Prestige streaming sci-fi / festival-friendly elevated genre
buyer_appeal.detail: The core concept can be sold off one lead performance and one strong director, because the story is contemporary, contained in spirit, and built around repeatable body-jump set pieces rather than expensive world-building. The body-swap hook, the romance, and the tech-satire angle give it a clear platform-friendly lane with strong trailer moments and exportable genre appeal.

considerations.area: The middle opens into many body-jump episodes.
considerations.detail: The sequence of host visits is one of the movie’s pleasures, but a next pass could consider which encounters are essential to the emotional arc and which could be folded together. The version where a few of the shorter jumps are combined would protect momentum while keeping the variety that makes the concept sing.

considerations.area: The final act carries a lot of geography.
considerations.detail: The Texas, Nebraska, chapel, stadium, and Grand Central material all adds scale and feeling, but it also expands the footprint quickly. One simplification lever would be to let one or two of those emotional beats happen in New York so the story keeps its sweep without asking for as many company moves.

considerations.area: Miles’s reveal can be sharpened even more.
considerations.detail: The script already gives Miles a strong ideological presence, and the later confession about feeling and perfection is compelling. A next pass could foreground one earlier moment where his personal need for control shows through the corporate polish, so the final confrontation lands with even more inevitability.

considerations.area: Sol’s interior life arrives through action.
considerations.detail: Sol is vivid and magnetic, and the body-jump banter gives them great surface energy. There is room to deepen the emotional contrast by letting one scene linger a little longer on what Sol is protecting underneath the bravado, which would make the final love story hit even harder.

considerations.area: The branded world needs a clearance pass.
considerations.detail: Budd-ee, the app language, the campaign slogans, and the named songs all help the movie feel specific and marketable. A producer would want to plan early for music and brand review so the script’s identity stays intact through production.

considerations.area: The lead performance is the package’s biggest asset.
considerations.detail: Because V has to play across so many bodies, the project benefits enormously from a performer with range, comic timing, and emotional precision. The version of the package that lands fastest is the one that pairs a distinctive director with a lead actor who can make the body-switching feel effortless.
